checks.finding: The actual level-zero class lattice is retained, not replaced by a model. Its local unitary descriptions give integrality, and the stored atT.disc quotient gives L^vee/L = O_E/T with index T^[E:Q]. The scalar extension uses rho=embE o CM conjugation o sigma_eTau. Its span is full, its Gram matrix is sigma rho(G), and bc_norm holds at every coefficient embedding. The nonempty class set follows from the stored class bijection.

The coefficient map uses the same Forms0 record and original divided-power Weyl lattice. For the action R(g)P=det(g)^s P(g^t Z), composition has the stated order. A p-local primal basis Y and its original dual basis are related by the literal transpose identity (rho(Y)^(-1)rho(G)^(-1))^t = (embT(Y*G))^(-1); the source's every-place/every-basis integral criterion therefore matches CV.fin. Signed determinant shifts are retained. Restriction to each original class justifies changing its archimedean frame separately. The resulting Fock sum, with original class weights 1, supplies the literal CV.inf.

The P_r derivative-contraction recurrence has the required minus sign. Subtracting it from the shifted L_r recurrence and antisymmetrizing cancels each contraction by the transposition of positions 1 and j. This proves the precise ordered Capelli determinant identity. The largest moved column kills the highest vector, giving the exact norm recurrence N_(nu+1)=product_i(nu_i+k-i+1)N_nu. Deleting the last row/column when nu_k=0 and the dimension-zero value determine the factorial/Vandermonde formula. The diagonal monomial coefficient is 1, so both hook inequalities have the correct normalization.

The integral coefficient lattice is exactly dual to the divided-power lattice for F/N_nu. Every coefficient monomial has the prescribed column sums, so its diagonal Gram weight is at least (k^d c_nu)^(-1). Cauchy-Binet and a nonzero integer minor give the determinant lower bound on the coefficient lattice; exact integral duality reverses it on the Weyl lattice. The resulting slope uses squared Gram determinants and therefore has no extra factor 1/2. The final scope clarification extends the IW5 argument across arbitrary determinant shifts and handles k=0 explicitly, so the full original StdSlopeLow predicate is matched.

For any supplied ColVal, bc extends to an isomorphism because its image contains the full Q lattice and both dimensions equal k. Diagonal norm equalities imply the full Hermitian identity by polarization using a nonreal element of the CM host. Scalar extension preserves normalized slope: local determinant valuations multiply by ramification, sum ef gives the extension degree, and archimedean embeddings repeat equally often. Hermitian duality reverses slope; the exact index T^(2f) then gives mu(Q)=-log(T)/k. This applies to arbitrary ColVal, not only the constructed one.

Permutation symmetry of row weights gives det(R(g))^k=det(g)^(r a) with the original signed weight sum a. Diagonal matrices and elementary unipotents suffice to verify the formula, and raising to the kth power avoids an unjustified fractional determinant. Tensor Gram determinants and the original class direct sum give the stated exact slope decomposition. The class count cancels after division by rank, and GLS5 yields the source SlopeLow.

The Euclidean form is B=Tr_(E/Q) h, without half-trace. For the original full lattice M=L_c^vee, its integer-pairing dual is exactly D_E^(-1)L_c, using O_E stability and the CM-invariant codifferent. For nonzero z in that dual, h(z,z) is totally positive and lies in D_E^(-2); ideal norm and AM-GM give lambda_1(M*) >= sqrt([E:Q])/rd(E). Banaszczyk's transference inequality in dimension n=[E:Q]k gives squared lengths <=[E:Q]k^2 rd(E)^2. Extracting k E-independent vectors and dividing by 2f=[E:Q] proves the literal ShortAt constant k^2(2v)^2. There is no extra factor two, T, or covolume term.

Short dual vectors give functionals integral on the exact O_K-span bc(L_c). Their coefficient map is injective on the same class component. At every finite place, the signed determinant factor converts the local coefficient condition to the fractional ideal I=product_tau(det M_tau)^(s_tau), including negative s_tau. The finite ideal slope and archimedean factor D_sigma=product |det X|^(2s) combine, via the exact Q slope, to -sum_tau s_tau log(T). No determinant twist or coefficient embedding is discarded.

The Hilbert-Schmidt squared norm of the substituted row-functional matrix equals the sum of the original short-vector Hermitian norms. The homogeneous symmetric-tensor model gives the Fock operator bound with exponent d, so the squared coefficient norm is bounded by D_sigma product_tau G_tau,sigma^d_tau. Averaging over coefficient embeddings gives exactly Trace/(2f); Jensen then yields log(k^3(2v)^2). The original ClassMapT/ClassMap ideal, coefficient, norm and determinant fields all match.

The maximum-slope comparison follows from a nonzero pseudo-basis minor, fractional-ideal norm, Cauchy-Binet, and the product formula, with the required factor 2 in finite degrees. Original class projections are integral and archimedean orthogonal, so the direct sum maximum bound is valid. The intermediate term d log(4k^4v^2) becomes 4d log(kv) because the original host gives v>=2; AH16 applies with f>=8. The signed determinant contribution is safely bounded by |s|log(T), with T>=2. Thus the exact constant C5=4 is justified.

Both slope predicates quantify universally over the supplied ColVal, so their family threshold is zero and no existence hypothesis is smuggled into them. The actual same-family second-layer record supplies ColsTiedSym, and inherited RSL7 gives adm3 pointwise. The common threshold max(a,b,Fm.x1+1) is chosen before members and words; it removes the strict x1 guard and gives the original unguarded tCV.

The literal eleven fields of FamGLmin are accounted for: h2b,h2v,h3 by inherited MF/RSL/DSZ; hZa,hZb,tCV by GLS12; hW,hmu by RSL; hI,hR,hB by the exact GLE results. They use the same class, family, selector and forms. Closed conjunction takes the minimum positive epsilon cutoff and componentwise supremum of TransportedAlt tuples before Fm and CH. FamU retains HidaSetting. TuSize is not needed merely to form these guarded fields, and the final linkGLOBAL7_min/items/link8 assembly is correctly retained as a separate B obligation.
